headline: The hard stamp has a ladder: warm v4 sits at 3/8, so there is still a game to win
lede: Stage 3c's training batch waits on a predictions answer until Nov 19, so slot a scored the row the matrix was missing — the BC warm start at the harder difficulty. It loses five of eight games there, and that gap is exactly what the eight-goal experiment needed.

notes.text: retrogames-rl PR #10 (98434c1): v4 at {slack,wizard} on validation 500..507 — 3/8 wins, avgLv 8.38, 22,740 ticks, hero deaths 55. The stamp's val ladder is now complete: cpu 8/8 | v4 3/8 | idle 0/8, all on a byte-identical sim (audited 6746faa..228f01c).

Win is NOT a dead signal at the hard stamp. The old bias verdict measured the CPU (8/8 even at the stamp) — but warm v4 wins only 3/8, so win-trained v2 models have real headroom against their own warm start, not just speed and survival.

The best behaviour-cloning model gets the hero killed more than an idle partner at hard settings (55 deaths vs 6.25, min hp −12%) despite winning more games. Pad accuracy 0.916 stops meaning good partner the moment the stamp makes the hero fragile — distance drift is what kills.
Every lane's step-1 park command could die halfway: `cp STATE.md A B` treats B as a directory, skipped fetch and detach on a stale HEAD. Fixed (PR #2547) — two copies, slot-scoped first.
